title: SIP Step-Up
blurb: Raising the SIP automatically each year: the two step-up types, who it suits, how to set it up and how to keep it realistic.

rows: New employees (all sections), sales team (talk-tracks, role-plays) and investors as awareness material
One 45–60 minute session, plus 15 minutes of role-play and the quiz
Module 9 (goal-based investing), Module 12 (SIP – What Next?) and Module 13 (Asset Allocation)
Each L.E.A.R.N. stage has: what to know, how to do it, a talk-track, and the investor takeaway
outcomes: Explain what a step-up (top-up) SIP is and the two ways to set it: a percentage or a fixed amount.
Show with illustrative numbers why stepping up matters more than most clients expect.
Check whether a client can afford a step-up, and pick a sensible rate.
Use a step-up to make a goal reachable from a lower starting SIP.
Review, pause or lower a step-up when life changes.
Handle the behaviour that blocks step-ups, within compliance.

sources: SBI Mutual Fund: Top-up SIP terms (minimum ₹500 in multiples of ₹500; half-yearly or yearly for monthly SIPs)
DSP Mutual Fund: terms for special facilities (fixed or percentage top-up; instalment capped at ₹5 lakh or the mandate limit)
AMFI distributor guidelines; AMC scheme forms for top-up and pause facilities
Income-tax Act and Finance Act provisions on capital gains from mutual funds (verify current rates each year)

lessons.title: Why a flat SIP isn't enough

a: Save more tomorrow, automatically. Tie each step-up to a raise, so the client never feels the money go.
A SIP whose instalment rises by a set amount or percentage at set intervals, decided once and applied by the AMC.
Adds the same rupee amount each time.
Remember: gentler and easier to budget.
Raises the instalment by a set percentage of the previous one.
Remember: grows faster, because each raise is on a bigger base.
Minimum ₹500, in multiples of ₹500; half-yearly or yearly for monthly SIPs; chosen at enrolment.
Fixed (from ₹500) or percentage; half-yearly or yearly; instalment capped at ₹5 lakh or the mandate limit.
At 6% inflation, ₹10,000 a month in 20 years buys only what about ₹3,100 buys today.
A flat SIP becomes a smaller share of income every year, without the client deciding anything.
Later, bigger instalments still have years to grow, so a step-up adds more than its rupee value suggests.
A 10% yearly step-up roughly doubles a long-term outcome, and invests far more in total.
Flat SIP: about ₹19,800 a month. With a 10% yearly step-up: about ₹11,500 to start. Illustrative at 12%.
Starting the 10% step-up five years late: ≈ ₹1.45 Cr instead of ≈ ₹1.99 Cr — about ₹54 lakh.
Income growth, emergency fund and loans, budget room, and time to the goal.
Step up at or below expected income growth: income +8–10% a year → a 5–10% step-up.
Retirees on fixed income, clients with very irregular earnings, and goals only 1–3 years away.
Pick the type; set a cap; check the mandate; check re-registration for an existing SIP; time it to the raise; or start a second SIP each year.
The maximum instalment, beyond which the step-up stops rising.
Example: cap at ₹20,000.
Remember: it turns an open commitment into a bounded one.
The maximum the bank will allow per debit.
Example: set at ₹25,000 for a SIP rising to ₹16,105.
Remember: it must cover the highest future instalment.
Adding a step-up to an existing SIP can mean cancelling and registering again.
Example: a 4-year-old SIP with no facility.
Remember: the instalment and exit-load clocks restart.
Check income, comfort, goal progress, the cap, the mandate limit and the asset mix.
Pay cut: pause, don't cancel. New EMI: hold the step-up. Big raise: a larger step-up. Goal near: send extra money to debt.
Spending rises with income; the SIP stays flat.
Example: the raise disappears into monthly spending.
Remember: send a slice of every raise to the SIP first.
Choosing a small gain now over a bigger one later.
Example: "I'll increase it next year."
Remember: automate it and the decision disappears.
Worrying about affording future instalments.
Example: "What if I can't afford it later?"
Remember: a cap plus a review date answers it.
Treating the first SIP as the right one forever.
Example: "₹10,000 is my SIP."
Remember: as a share of income it is much smaller now.
Delaying a step-up until markets "settle".
Example: "I'll step up after the correction."
Remember: a step-up is about income, not the market.
Label projections illustrative; show the total invested; explain cap, mandate and re-registration; record consent.
Save more tomorrow, automatically. A step-up decided once beats good intentions every year.

questions.q: What is a step-up SIP?
o: A SIP that rises automatically at set intervals
A SIP that switches funds every year
A SIP with a guaranteed return
questions.why: The instalment rises by a fixed amount or a percentage at a set interval, decided once and applied by the AMC.

questions.q: A fixed-amount step-up adds…
o: The same rupee amount each time
A percentage of the previous instalment
questions.why: A fixed amount adds the same rupees each time; a percentage raises the instalment by a share of a growing base.

questions.q: Starting from ₹10,000, what is the third instalment under a 10% yearly step-up?
questions.why: ₹10,000 → ₹11,000 → ₹12,100. Each raise is 10% of the previous instalment.

questions.q: Name the two ways a step-up can be set.
questions.why: A fixed rupee amount each time, or a percentage of the previous instalment.

questions.q: What is SBI Mutual Fund's top-up minimum and multiple?
questions.why: At least ₹500, in multiples of ₹500, half-yearly or yearly for monthly SIPs.

questions.q: At DSP Mutual Fund, the step-up instalment is capped at…
o: ₹5 lakh or the bank mandate limit, whichever is lower
questions.why: ₹5 lakh or the mandate limit, whichever is lower. Terms differ by AMC, so always check the form.

questions.q: A step-up facility is often available only on…
o: An existing SIP of five years or more
questions.why: Many AMCs offer it only on a fresh registration, so converting an existing SIP may mean re-registering.

questions.q: Adding a step-up to an existing SIP can mean cancelling and re-registering. What does that do?
o: It resets the instalment clock and the exit-load period on new units
questions.why: A new registration means new instalment dates and a new exit-load clock. Explain it before acting.

questions.q: Why show the total invested beside the final value?
o: Because a step-up invests far more, and showing only the result misleads
questions.why: A 10% step-up invests about ₹68.7 L instead of ₹24 L in the illustration. Both numbers belong on the page.

questions.q: What step-up rate is usually comfortable?
o: At or below expected income growth, often 5–10%
Above income growth, to catch up
questions.why: At or below expected income growth. A step-up faster than income growth squeezes the budget within a few years.

questions.q: A goal is 1–3 years away. What does a step-up add?
o: A great deal; step up aggressively
Little, and extra money may need to move to debt instead
questions.why: Under three years a step-up adds little, and the money should be moving towards debt.

questions.q: The AMC offers no step-up facility, or the client wants control. What is the alternative?
o: Starting a second, smaller SIP each year
questions.why: A second SIP each year gives the same effect with more flexibility.

questions.q: In the illustration, what does a 10% step-up do to a ₹10,000, 20-year SIP?
o: Roughly doubles the value, from about ₹1.0 Cr to about ₹2.0 Cr, with far more invested
Has no effect without a longer tenure
questions.why: About ₹1.99 Cr against ₹1.0 Cr, with about ₹68.7 L invested instead of ₹24 L.

questions.q: The 15% step-up row invests about ₹1.23 Cr. Why is it risky to recommend?
o: It needs the largest income growth and is the most likely to be cancelled
The AMC does not allow it
questions.why: It requires income to keep up for twenty years. A cancelled step-up is worse than a modest one.

questions.q: Which is the honest way to present a step-up illustration?
o: The final value, the total invested, and the assumed return labelled illustrative
A guarantee of the final value
A comparison with a fixed deposit only
questions.why: All three, every time: the result, the extra money invested, and the assumption.

questions.q: In the illustration, starting the 10% step-up five years late costs about…
questions.why: About ₹54 lakh: ₹1.45 Cr against ₹1.99 Cr when the step-up starts in year 2.

questions.q: A client says a step-up feels like too much commitment. What helps?
o: A cap, plus the option to pause or reduce at review
questions.why: A cap bounds the commitment, and a review date makes it revisitable.

questions.q: A client receives a ₹4 lakh bonus. What is the right order?
o: Bonus into the SIP, then the emergency fund
Emergency fund and loans first, then a lump sum or STP alongside the step-up
Cancel the SIP and invest the bonus
Use the bonus instead of a step-up
questions.why: Basics first. A bonus is irregular; the step-up is the annual habit, so use both.

questions.q: Name two checks before suggesting a step-up.
o: Income growth and the emergency fund
The fund's star rating and the AMC's AUM
The market level and the tax rate
The number of folios and the nominee
questions.why: Income growth, the emergency fund and loans, budget room, and the time to the goal.

questions.q: The bank mandate is lower than the highest future instalment. What should happen?
o: Raise the mandate when the step-up is set up
questions.why: A mandate that only covers today's amount will fail later, and three consecutive failures cancel a monthly SIP.

questions.q: When is the step-up reviewed?
o: At the annual SIP review, alongside the goal and the asset mix
questions.why: It is part of the annual review: income, comfort, goal progress, cap, mandate and asset mix.

questions.q: Which client does a percentage step-up suit least?
o: A retiree on a fixed pension
A business owner whose income grows
questions.why: A fixed pension does not grow, so the instalment would rise while income does not.

questions.q: A step-up faster than income growth will…
o: Squeeze the budget within a few years and get cancelled or missed
questions.why: The instalment becomes a visibly larger share of pay, and the client either cancels it or starts missing debits.

questions.q: What is lifestyle creep?
o: Spending rising with income while the SIP stays flat
The SIP amount rising every year
questions.why: It is why a flat SIP quietly becomes a smaller share of income.

questions.q: What is present bias in the step-up conversation?
o: Preferring a small gain now over a larger one later, as in "I'll increase it next year"
questions.why: It is beaten by automation: set the step-up now and it happens on its own.

questions.q: Which statement is compliant?
o: "Illustratively, at 12% assumed, a 10% step-up invests about ₹68.7 L and could reach about ₹2 crore; not guaranteed."
questions.why: Label it illustrative, state the assumption and the total invested, and promise nothing.

questions.q: For ₹1 crore in 15 years at an assumed 12%, what is the starting SIP with and without a 10% step-up?
o: About ₹19,800 flat; about ₹11,500 with the step-up
About ₹11,500 flat; about ₹19,800 with the step-up
About ₹25,000 flat; about ₹15,000 with the step-up
questions.why: About ₹19,800 flat, or about ₹11,500 to start with a 10% yearly step-up. Illustrative, not a promise.

questions.q: What must be recorded after agreeing a step-up?
o: The rule (type, rate, frequency), the cap, the mandate limit and the review date
questions.why: The note is the record of consent, and it drives the next review.

questions.q: A step-up is a decision about…
questions.why: It is tied to income growth, not to a market view. Falls are good months to buy more units.

questions.q: ₹15,000 flat vs ₹10,000 with a 10% step-up over 20 years: what does the illustration show?
o: ₹1.50 Cr vs ₹1.99 Cr, with ₹36.0 L vs ₹68.7 L invested
₹1.99 Cr vs ₹1.50 Cr, with ₹36.0 L vs ₹68.7 L invested
questions.why: The flat SIP reaches about ₹1.50 Cr from ₹36 L invested; the step-up reaches about ₹1.99 Cr from ₹68.7 L.
